title: Membrane Arena: a browser game about three coupled membranes, reward schemes, a shield, an amplifier and a stabilizer (SYNTHETIC classical simulation)
description: SYNTHETIC educational game, zero dependencies, offline, English and French. The player steers three coupled Oja-rule membranes that learn a planted pattern in noise, chooses a reward scheme, a cooperation setting, a 2-of-3 shield, a capped amplifier and a gain-clamped stabilizer, and watches a (1+1) evolution step. Scores are compared with the measured width-32 results of the crystallization-contest repository, with the source file cited next to each number. Includes a daily seeded contest, a plain-text share card and challenge links in the URL hash, and a Lab view with instruments, multi-seed ensembles with confidence intervals against the repository baselines, paired A/B tests and a replay. A brain page sizes layers of membranes with the 2f + 1 rule and joins them with delayed links called microtubules (a metaphor only; nothing models real neurons, microtubules or a brain), and the Quorum Keeper logic game builds and breaks such fault-tolerant brains against an exhaustive adversary; its level targets are tuned to each level's own seed. Reverse Membranes runs the arena backwards at width 16: membranes with the learning sign flipped (anti-Hebbian) find a dark direction whose energy was removed from every observation; "opposite energy" is only the name of a score, and nothing models negative energy, antimatter, physics or biology. Reverse Pair joins a reverse observer and a predictable calibrator that plays signed-amplitude sine tones on one clock, with an equalizer and a 2-membrane shield, and ships a frozen evaluation protocol: thresholds tuned on calibration seeds, results on 120 held-out seeds with bootstrap intervals and paired effect sizes, on-grid and off-grid fades, baselines and an oracle, and one command that regenerates every number with SHA-256 hashes; nothing models oscillators or radio hardware. Pair Watch turns Reverse Pair into a visual game where the player is the second vote of the 2-membrane shield, with a logistic coach fitted on calibration runs and frozen, evaluated under its own frozen protocol on 200 held-out runs (calibration error and paired points with bootstrap intervals), and replay codes checked by replaying the seed. Wave Pulse sends a ripple across a 40 x 26 damped wave grid and asks the player to locate its start from edge-sensor arrival times, against a least-squares locator calibrated on 200 pulses and evaluated under its own frozen protocol on 200 held-out pulses in 16 settings (locator error, coverage of its 90% region, bootstrap intervals and Holm-corrected tests); nothing models a real floor, pressure waves or holography. Classical simulation only: the JavaScript port is statistically comparable to the Python original, not bit-identical. No accounts, no network calls.
